page.layout: One column of running text, with an engraved armillary-sphere diagram in the middle; a signature "G 4" and catchword "que" at the foot right. The digitiser's banner "http://rcin.org.pl" at the bottom is left out.

main_text.l: In secundo situ, si terra in Axe quidem, sed
non in medio mundi locata esset, hæc sequerentur
I. In omni climate planum Horizontis secaret
cœlum in duas æquales partes, exceptis locis
diuideretur in duos æquales arcus, & sic alicu-
bi plus, alicubi minus sex signis de zodiaco conspi-
Occidetis solis non congruerent, ita ut in una recta linea
seu ἐπ' εὐθείας consisterent. Nec umbra
orientis solis die solstitiali, rectam lineam constitueret cum um-
bra Solis occidentis die brumali & econuerso.
In tertio situ, Si neq; in axe mundi sita esset, ne-que

page.notes: Engraving of an armillary sphere with zodiac signs and sun/star markings, centre of the page; not transcribed. Roman numerals I. and II. are paragraph numbers, not headings. Greek phrase "ἐπ' εὐθείας" reproduced from the scan as best read; the printed Greek is "ἐπ' εὐθείας" with a leading "ξ" word-break mark, uncertain. Lower page is damaged by staining; the word "que" catchword is read from the foot right.
